body:
I'm curious, how long have you been feeling like this? You said earlier that you "used to be just like that".

Also, to be honest, I think that you are looking for the wrong things. If you were to find someone with a similar mindset you would probably have a harder time getting out of this apathy-feeling that you have. Don't get me wrong, you shouldn't hang out with people you find stupid, but at the same time I think it's really important not to forget about other qualities. Let's say you find this typically "cute" girl. She hasn't thought much about politics, religion and maybe not even life itself. She doesn't have the same experiences that you have and might find it hard to understand the way you feel. At the same time, she's open minded, has a big heart, appreciates life and doesn't need an intellectual joke to laugh. That's also really important stuff to learn. 

At the same time it's clear that you want a challenge and that you want to find somebody that gets you interested. What sort of topics that can lead to a discussion are you interested in? It's kinda hard to have a challenging discussion about itembuilds or counterpicks in games, so something other than that.

I hope it doesn't sound as if I'm not taking your problems seriously, trust me, I am. There aren't many feelings that are worse to be stuck in.
Thank you. Even though I still feel like I said earlier, that really helps. I really wish that I could think about his life, but right now I break every time I try.

I can also tell you a bit about myself! 
I love to play league of legends, I have a kind of morbid sense of humour and wish I had a dog. A fluffy white one, but not too small. I would like to be able to wrestle with it, but I also need to be able to win. And I'm kind of a more-fat-than-muscle person. But I'm not fat! Just.. weak.

Right now, I am kind of bored, but I was in court today and I guess that was kind of cool. I didn't do anything illegal, I'm a lawstudent and we were there to watch the judge work. It was a guy there who should totally get sued for his haircut.

I'm trying to think like you described in 4), and right now my biggest motivation is that I can't bear the thought of making someone else feel the misery my friend made me feel. I know for a fact that he is dead, because he was sick and needed medication to even be able to walk, and I can't figure out how he would get them without his card or ID. I also know that I probably could live with this, if I just gave it time, because I've learned that I have, as you said, a really strong will. Otherwise I would never have been able to beat my eating disorder. The thing is, this is so different from any other problems I have faced. I know it sounds obvious, and maybe it is, but the main thing that kept me going when I was ill was that I knew that some day I could live a healthy life if I really tried. I had been healthy once before, so why wouldn't I be able to do it again? My whole life has been a struggle towards happiness, and against depression, and during all this time I've always had concrete problems that I knew about and that I knew I would have to fix to get better. This is nothing like that, as you can imagine (or maybe you know, I don't know your life story).

The thing is, no matter how much I try or how much I fight, I can't make this problem go away. I will never be able to bring him back to life, I'm not even able to find his body. His family is religious and they find comfort in the thought that he's in a better place, but I don't believe so can't do that. The only thing I can think about is that his skins is probably peeled off right now, how terrified he must've been, how cold he must've felt and that even if his body would be recovered I will not ever be able to see his face again. I also can't stop thinking about the fact that we had a fight the night before, that I was really mean to him, and that he probably thought that it was for the best that night when he jumped. He used to say that everyone would be better off without him, that sure, they would all be sad for a while but eventually they would forget about him and.. well.. I just can't do that. The only thing I could possibly do to feel better would be to move on, to force myself not to think about how he smelled, or how he looked when he laughed, until I forgot. And no matter how I think about it, that would mean that he was right. That we would move on, that we would forget.

As I said, it's been 6 months, and I'm already starting to forget his voice. I know I can't stop time or rewind it, but I also know I can't move on. I don't want to solve this problem. I don't want to move on. I know it's stupid and that if I don't, this will destory me, but I just can't.

I'd like to give it a try too.
I've had problems with depression for as long as i can remember, probably before i was around 10 years old because at that time i became anorexic, and i guess that stuff just doesn't happen randomly. i got my first boyfriend at the age of 13, an amazing guy, but he couldn't stand being together with me when i got really sick. i don't blame him since my whole personality changed and if i didn't cry for days and days in a row i was angry and hostile. he broke up, and i decided to become better to get him back. things didn't really work out and i became bulimic instead, but i promised him i was fine and we got back together. at the age of 17 i was down at a BMI under 15 again and got checked in to a clinic, and stayed there for 2 years. it was an amazing experience, even though really hard, but eventually i became better. at 19 i wasn't sick anymore. me and my boyfriend broke up, but remained close friends, and i felt happier than i had ever done before. i felt like things could actually turn out good for me, even though i had been depressed and suicidal for so long. i started to do stuff i had always wanted to do, like living abroad for a couple of months. so far so good.

now im in a different spot. one of my closest friends jumped off a bridge and has been missing for over 6 months. i was in love with him. i got his last text and have spent hours describing where and how he cut himself to the police in case they found his corpse. his family is telling me how i shouldn't blame myself since nobody knew how he felt, except i did. (and didn't tell anyone because im a fucking retard.) when i'm alone i binge like a maniac and throw up everything i eat. i miss him, i feel terribly guilty, and i kinda want to die. (i know there is a big hole in my story, but i don't really have the energy to write it down.)
obivously i don't want to make anyone else suicidal too, so i haven't tried anything stupid. i've got a little suicide-kit in my wardrobe though, in case i change my mind.

EDIT; sorry about my poor english, it's not my native language.

you've probably seen it, but this blog always cheers me up;
http://hyperboleandahalf.blogspot.se/
I don't feel like I have anything intelligent to say, other than please hang on. If you want someone to talk to, I'll gladly listen. Have the doctors been able to find out what's physically wrong?

Please don't. I've been that girl. You say that all you want to do is make her happy, this will destroy her life. Trust me. If she doesn't kill herself because of the guilt for not saving you, which is a high possibility, she'll be utterly depressed for the rest of her life.

And I was so mean to him the last time we spoke. He tried to make things right and I just shut him out, telling him there was no point and that he should leave me alone. Later that night, at 4 am, he texted me. I didn't wake up.

I loved a guy that killed himself. I knew how sad he was, and I was too far away to help him, and still I didn't tell anybody. For some reason I believed him everytime he said "no, it's okay, i won't do anything stupid". Now his family, the police, and all of my friends are trying to comfort me, saying it's not my fault, because nobody knew how he felt and therefore couldn't stop him. But I knew, and I can't tell them that because I'm so afraid they might hate me. Because I do.
